items.label: Acknowledging the other person's stated feelings
items.description: Statements in my messages that name, acknowledge or accept a feeling the other person expressed.

anchors.1: OTHER expresses a feeling and no ME message acknowledges it.
anchors.3: One brief acknowledgement of OTHER's feeling (for example 'that sucks').
anchors.5: Several ME messages name or accept OTHER's feeling and stay with it.

items.speaker: me

items.label: Shifting the topic to myself
items.description: Statements in my messages that move the conversation from what the other person shared to my own experience.

anchors.1: ME responds to what OTHER shared and stays on OTHER's topic.
anchors.3: ME briefly shifts to their own experience, then returns to OTHER's topic.
anchors.5: ME moves the conversation to their own experience and does not return to OTHER's topic.

items.speaker: me

items.label: Statements assigning fault to the other person
items.description: Statements in my messages that say the other person caused a problem or is to blame.

anchors.1: No ME message assigns fault to OTHER.
anchors.3: One ME statement assigns fault to OTHER.
anchors.5: Several ME statements assign fault to OTHER.

items.speaker: me

items.label: Statements taking responsibility for a problem
items.description: Statements in my messages that accept responsibility for a problem or a mistake.

anchors.1: No ME message accepts responsibility for anything.
anchors.3: One partial acceptance (for example 'I could have texted').
anchors.5: A clear, specific acceptance of responsibility.

items.speaker: me

items.label: Raising intensity during a disagreement
items.description: Sharper wording, sweeping statements or dismissive replies in my messages during a disagreement.

anchors.1: During the disagreement ME keeps the same or a calmer tone.
anchors.3: Some sharper wording or one dismissive reply from ME.
anchors.5: Repeated sharp, sweeping or dismissive ME statements.

items.speaker: me

items.label: Repair attempts after friction
items.description: Apologies, reassurance, humor or proposals to talk later in my messages after friction.

anchors.1: Friction occurs and ME makes no repair attempt.
anchors.3: One brief repair attempt (short apology, joke, softer tone).
anchors.5: A clear repair: apology or reassurance plus a proposal to reconnect.

limitations: This is not a diagnosis, an assessment or a test, and it cannot detect any condition.
It describes patterns in one text conversation only, not who you or the other person are.
Text messages miss tone of voice, context, and everything said in person or on calls.
Word rates and reply times are descriptive counts with no normal range and no cutoffs.
Reply times are approximate: notifications, sleep and busy days all change them.
AI-scored items can be wrong; items whose two scoring runs disagreed were left out.
Quotes are short excerpts and can read differently out of context.
